newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bill to shed light on Brazil's telecoms selloff.
newsitem.headline: Bill to shed light on Brazil's telecoms selloff.

text.p: A broad new law fixing guidelines for Brazil's telecoms sector should clarify government plans to privatize the federally owned Telebras system, analysts said.
"This law will allow private players into conventional telephone services and should provide details on the Telebras system's privatization," said Maxim Medvedovsky, an analyst with Banco Icatu.

A bill containing the comprehensive new General Telecommunications Law is expected to be submitted to Congress's lower house this week, although no date has been set yet, a Communications Ministry spokesman said.

The bill, which also would create a regulatory body, rules for conventional telephone services and a broad structure for the sector, will be closely watched by investors eyeing Brazil's mammoth telecoms sector, analysts said.
"The market will be very nervous when the document is published," said Jacopo Valentino of German bank Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's local unit.
But even with fast-track status, the bill could spend months in the lower house and Senate before becoming law.
"We would like to get a vote in the Chamber of Deputies in January and possibly in the Senate in March or April," ministry spokesman Francisco Mendonca said.
Among key items expected to be contained in the new law, which will cover cellular, satellite or cable services whose guidelines were approved in a mini-law last month, are:
* Creation of a politically independent regulatory body, whose decisions may only be overturned by a court.
* A broad outline of the industry's structure, including telephone, broadcasting and other communication-related services, aimed at stimulating competition.
* Rules guiding the transition from a state monopoly to a privately run sector grounded in open competition, including authorization for Telebras' pre-privatization restructuring.
The law is unlikely to set out a timeframe or define the privatization model for Telebras, South America's largest telecom with a market capitalization of about $20 billion, analysts said.
But it is expected to shed light on Telebras' pre-selloff break-up, possibly into four to six "Baby Bras'," they said.
It also may stipulate some guarantees for minority shareholders, they added. "An explicit statement in this sense would have a positive impact on the market," one said.
Initial confusion over the telecoms law, due to its likely complexity, may cause a drop in telecoms shares but most analysts remain upbeat on the sector in light of privatization.
